newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portuguese commonwealth stuck on shoestring budget.
newsitem.headline: Portuguese commonwealth stuck on shoestring budget.

text.p: The recently-launched commonwealth of Portuguese-speaking countries is powerless to do anything because it has hardly any money, its senior official Marcolino Moco was quoted as saying on Thursday.
"The budget isn't enough to do anything," the former Angolan prime minister told Portugal's Valor magazine in an interview.

The Community of Portuguese-Speaking Countries (CPLP) was launched amid fanfare in July to promote cooperation between Portugal and its former colonies of Brazil, Angola, Mozambique, Guinea-Bissau, Cape Verde and Sao Tome & Principe.

The Lisbon-based community, an echo of the larger British Commonwealth and Francophone group, aims to defend Portuguese as an international language and tighten political and diplomatic ties between member states.

Moco said the CPLP, which has a small staff, was struggling along on a $400,000 annual budget and depended on contributions from local embassies. Portugal and Brazil are the main contributors to its budget.
